item.title: Re: Staff Post - Open
item.content:encoded:
It was never my intention to be mean spirited in this proposal. Linking to to the D Comm articles just seemed like a natural step given how this article basically catalogs them. However, I do have to say you make a very valid point in that we should be linking to high quality content. As such, an updated proposal follows:

+ Show Block
- Hide Block

The decommissioning tales associated with these are highly rated, so rather than linking to the articles themselves, I propose linking to those tales an supplements.

SCP-083-D could link to Duke till Dawn.
SCP-1016-D could link to Termination Log SCP-1016
SCP-531-D could link to Termination Order

The link would be in the same manner as described above.

You are right that ideally we are to be linking into newer material on the site, however, given that DComms are a relic of the 2008 and 2009 era, with no real analogue in the newer material, I think linking to these tales/supplements is an alright substitute.

Of course, as with all our suggestions we are open to hearing alternatives from any and all readers, so if there are any DComm analogues in more recent material, I'm all ears.

item.title: Moderator Post - Open
item.content:encoded:
Noting that a recent addition to this page was removed, as it introduced substantial new material without author or staff permission.

Grammatical edits are appreciated, but remember that if a page is not tagged with "collaboration", only the original author may make edits that consist of more than spelling/punctuation/grammar fixes. As such, while punctuation and spelling can be corrected, you should obtain author permission prior to adding new content yourself.

Furthermore, given that this is not the first time staff has needed to revert an unauthorized edit on this article, the page is now locked. Anyone wishing to add a new entry should post in the discussion here and/or contact the original author for permission.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
We don't mock merely bad writing forever. Collections such as this are reserved for the hilariously bad. The things so over-the-top terrible that literally anyone could have told the authors wouldn't work.

If your ideas are even marginally original, they almost certianly won't end up here. We may not like them, at least one person is certain to hate them and tell you exactly why in detail, but the worst treatment that 99% of unpopular ideas get is deletion and oblivion, never to be recalled for good or ill.

On the other hand, if you post you're iffy idea we might surprise you. I thought my first article (252) was pretty borderline, with difficult to read formatting and a pretty transparent gimick. I fully expected it to be deleted and was only hoping for a learning experience. But the feedback was almost universally positive, and here it sits at about +80 to this day.

I guess what I'm saying is that you shouldn't let our contempt of contemptible articles discourage you. Take 100-J for what it's meant to be, a joke. And perhaps some examples of what to avoid.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Part of the problem with my own writing ability is that the only memorable things I think up are things that are a part of me (with maybe three exceptions). Because of this, every one of them comes off as ridiculous (I have wisely refrained from writing anything up on this site) and is bashed into oblivion, and others are not only insulting my creations, but insulting me in the process. While I realize that this site has a much larger number of "critiques" as opposed to "merciless overly-harsh insulting of the entire concept of the work" (on some sites I posted, I just got a bunch of insults, curses, and slurs strung together into run-on sentences, thank 343 for the decent administration here), any insult of the general idea of the work feels like an insult to me personally by extension, because my only good work is the work that is a part of me.
And that is why I will probably never write an SCP all by myself. The idea that a part of me would be not only bashed into oblivion but also posted in an article like this so that people could continue to mock me throughout eternity doesn't make me feel any better about trying.

Of course, perhaps the clinical tone of this site would work in my favor, as I probably wouldn't NEED to develop any memorable character/thingy, because clinical reports do not comment on personality.

Still, I think I'm with Light on this one. It appears that if you make an article that uses an edgy, borderline idea (i.e. the ones here), you'll get bashed and mocked forever; in other words, it sort of sounds like "all the good ideas have already been taken" (I know it's not true, but I've looked over the entire SCP listings in the past few months, every single one, and most of my ideas have already been done, and I'm having a hard time of thinking up something new and original that doesn't come off as a pathetic self-insert or stupid "ogm so amazing" badassry.) I'll post more about my rejected ideas in the forum somewhere.

item.content:encoded:
Yes, this article might offend some people, and is a rather distasteful joke by itself.

Now, not deleting bad articles would be senseless. Even if you were to assume that space availability isn't an issue, said articles would be downvoted and mocked massively. It would be even more humiliating for the authors.

As for your comment about refusing new ideas, if you excuse the poor language: Bullshit. That's just a lame excuse. We don't loathe things such as OTT guns and Sue-ish furries because they're "new" ideas (They're not): We delete them because most are overused concepts based on wish fulfillment, which not only fail to fit the Foundation's universe but are also, usually, nowhere near as well written as they would need to be in order to convey interest or amusement of any sort.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
See, to me, this article is everything that's wrong about this site. Don't get me wrong, I love almost all of the articles and celebrating creativity is a brilliant thing.

But some of the more senior users here (it would be exceedingly impolite to give names) seem to be rather inflexible in their ways of thinking, and resistant to new ideas, which I think is a real shame.

And this article is a perfect example of that. Yes, no doubt there are some terrible SCPs written. If it were me, I wouldn't even delete them (is server space such an issue?) as people can simply not read articles they dislike but quietly deleting is perfectly fine and causes only mild hurt. But this… this feels like revisiting your high school to find a wall covered in old essays on which the teachers have written scathing abuse.

I think this just discourages creativity, as Light said, and personally I think you ought to be ashamed for finding it amusing.
